t.4.50.1: Having spoken thus, Hanumān there once again addressed that greatly blessed female ascetic, clad in black antelope skin and devoted to dharma.
t.4.50.2: We have rashly entered this cave shrouded in darkness, worn out by hunger and thirst and utterly exhausted in every way.
t.4.50.3: Tormented by thirst, we entered this great cavern of the earth; but having seen these wondrous things of so many kinds, we are distressed, bewildered and robbed of our senses.
t.4.50.4: Whose are these golden trees, gleaming like the newly risen sun? And whose are these pure roots and fruits, fit to be eaten?
t.4.50.5: There were golden palaces and silver houses, with windows of refined gold and covered with lattices of gems.
t.4.50.6: These trees made of gold, in full bloom and laden with fruit, holy and fragrant with sweet scent, by whose power do they exist?
t.4.50.7: How have golden lotuses sprung up in the clear water, and how do golden fish move about together with tortoises?
t.4.50.8: Who you are, what your power is, and whose ascetic might this is: since none of us knows, you should tell us everything.
t.4.50.9: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the female ascetic, who walked the path of dharma and delighted in the welfare of all beings, replied to Hanumān.
t.4.50.10: There was a mighty, illustrious bull among the Dānavas named Maya, a master of magic; by him, through his magic power, this entire golden forest was created.
t.4.50.11: In days of old there was, indeed, a Viśvakarmā of the foremost Dānavas, by whom this divine, golden, most excellent mansion was built.
t.4.50.12: He, having practised austerities for thousands of years in the great forest, obtained from Pitāmaha a boon: all the wealth of Uśanas.
t.4.50.13: Having arranged everything, the mighty one, master of all desires, then dwelt happily for some time in this great forest.
t.4.50.14: That bull among Dānavas, who was attached to the apsaras Hemā, the lord Puraṃdara slew, striding forth and seizing his thunderbolt.
t.4.50.15: This excellent forest was given by Brahmā to Hemā, together with the everlasting enjoyment of all desires and this golden mansion.
t.4.50.16: I am the daughter of Merusāvarṇi, and I myself, Prabhā, guard this dwelling of hers, of Hemā, O best of monkeys.
t.4.50.17: Hemā, skilled in dance and song, is my dear friend. Granted a boon by her, I guard this excellent mansion.
t.4.50.18: What is your purpose, or for what reason do you enter these wildernesses? And how was this impassable forest discovered by you?
t.4.50.19: Having eaten these edible roots and fruits and having drunk the water, you should tell me everything.
